title: Mosaic stitch box lid
subtitle: A small 12 cm square box lid panel in three-colour mosaic stitch on 13-count canvas
excerpt: This box lid panel uses alternating mosaic stitch blocks in three colours on 13-count canvas to produce a diagonal tile effect. Finished size is 12 by 12 cm. The canvas is laced over a thin lid blank, which can be fitted to a plain wooden box.
sourceNotes: Mosaic stitch construction from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Three-colour tile arrangement synthesised from geometric canvaswork examples in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: A plain wooden or card box lid cut to receive a needlepoint panel. The canvas is laced over the lid and the box is then assembled around it.

heroPrompt: A small square wooden box with a needlepoint lid in dark green, cream and gold mosaic stitch tile pattern, on a writing desk with a pen and letter, natural light.

content.text: This box lid panel is a 62 by 62 hole square on 13-count canvas, finishing at 12 by 12 cm. Each mosaic stitch block occupies a 2 by 2 hole area in three stitches. The three-colour cycling arrangement: dark, medium, light: places the colours in a diagonal chequerboard that makes the mosaic block structure visible.
What you need

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 22 by 22 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin around the 62 by 62 hole design area)

items.label: Thread: dark
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3345 / Anchor 268 (dark hunter green). About 6 m

items.label: Thread: medium
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3346 / Anchor 267 (hunter green). About 5 m

items.label: Thread: light
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 3348 / Anchor 264 (light yellow green). About 5 m

items.label: Box lid blank
items.value: Thin board or plain wooden lid, 12 by 12 cm. Available from craft suppliers or cut from mountboard

items.label: Strong thread
items.value: Linen or button thread for lacing

content.text: Palette
Dark: DMC 3345 / Anchor 268: dark hunter green
Medium: DMC 3346 / Anchor 267: hunter green
Light: DMC 3348 / Anchor 264: light yellow green
Stretching the canvas
Mount on a hoop or small scroll frame. The diagonal mosaic stitch distorts the canvas moderately; a frame prevents the square panel from pulling into a diamond shape.
Stitches used
Mosaic stitch
: three-stitch diagonal blocks over a 2 by 2 hole area (short stitch over 1, long stitch over 2, short stitch over 1). Work the blocks in diagonal rows across the canvas.
Working method
Mark the 62 by 62 hole boundary. Work from the top-left corner. Place the first mosaic block in the dark shade.
Place the adjacent block in the medium shade. The third block in the row uses the light shade. Cycle: dark, medium, light, dark, medium, light across each diagonal row.
Work in diagonal rows from the top-left corner to the bottom-right. Each row shifts the colour sequence on by one step.
Block by dampening and pinning square to a board overnight.
Finishing
Trim the canvas margin to 2 cm. Lace the canvas over the
box lid blank

by threading lacing thread back and forth across the back of the lid in both directions, pulling the canvas taut. Glue the canvas margin to the underside with PVA glue if a flat underside is required for fitting a box.
What to try next
Scotch stitch uses the same 2 by 2 block structure but with a five-stitch square block. This gives a larger tile and a different balance of dark to light.
